meta.title: Reasoning Loop Guard
meta.description: Cuts a reasoning-loop attempt short and stops the retries, so a session does not stall for tens of minutes.

loopGuard.title: Loop guard
loopGuard.intro: When the model falls into a reasoning loop, the host retries the same deterministic failure over and over (1-5 minutes each). The guard cuts that attempt short once a loop is detected and stops further retries.
loopGuard.enableHint: When off, nothing is interfered with: no attempt is cut short.
loopGuard.thresholdsHint: Click Save to apply; invalid values are reported here and no request is sent.
loopGuard.limitHint: Consecutive reasoning chunks above this in one attempt count as a loop (integer >= 100).
loopGuard.budgetHint: Entered in seconds (>= 10); stored in milliseconds.
loopGuard.stallHint: Abort when no chunk arrives for this long (counted before the first chunk too). Default 180s.
loopGuard.noOutputHint: Abort when the stream keeps trickling reasoning but never produces text or tool calls. Default 600s. This is the rule most likely to misfire — a legitimately long think also has no output.
loopGuard.repeatWindowHint: Only look for repetition within this many recent characters (integer 1000-200000). Default 6000
loopGuard.repeatMinCharsHint: Minimum character gate for the criteria, replacing the old "window must be full" precondition; no repetition is judged below this many characters. Integer 500 to the window size. Default 1000
loopGuard.repeatMinLinesHint: Do not judge below this many non-empty lines (integer 5-5000). Default 30
loopGuard.repeatCyclesHint: Judge only when the most frequent line appears at least this many times (integer 2-100). Default 6
loopGuard.repeatUniqueRatioHint: Judge only when the unique-line ratio is <= this value (0.01-0.9). Default 0.2
loopGuard.repeatGramRatioHint: For long single-line / few-line output (under 30 lines) the window is split into non-overlapping 8-character fragments; judge when the unique-fragment ratio is <= this value (0.01-0.9). Default 0.10. A single-line block always has a unique-line ratio of 1.0, so this is its only fallback. Warning: raising it misfires more easily on long single-line natural language — measured Chinese prose single line ~0.36, English ~0.45, while genuinely degenerate single lines are only 0.007-0.009.
loopGuard.repeatNote: This rule catches a stream repeating the same short piece of text (especially common inside reasoning): when a window holds far more lines than unique lines it cuts the attempt short instead of waiting for the model to stop by itself; long single-line / few-line output is caught by the fragment uniqueness (k-gram) fallback instead.
loopGuard.retriesHint: How many retries the host may still do after a cut (integer 0-5).
loopGuard.lowerEffortHint: Drop the reasoning effort for corrective retries so the loop does not repeat.
loopGuard.invalidLimit: Reasoning chunk limit must be an integer >= 100
loopGuard.invalidBudget: Attempt time budget must be at least 10 seconds
loopGuard.invalidStall: Stall timeout must be an integer ≥ 10 seconds
loopGuard.invalidNoOutput: No-output timeout must be an integer ≥ 10 seconds
loopGuard.invalidRepeatWindow: Repetition window must be an integer between 1000 and 200000
loopGuard.invalidRepeatMinChars: Minimum character gate must be an integer between 500 and the repetition window
loopGuard.invalidRepeatMinLines: Minimum lines in window must be an integer between 5 and 5000
loopGuard.invalidRepeatCycles: Minimum repetition cycles must be an integer between 2 and 100
loopGuard.invalidRepeatUniqueRatio: Max unique-line ratio must be a number between 0.01 and 0.9
loopGuard.invalidRepeatGramRatio: Fragment uniqueness cap must be a number between 0.01 and 0.9
loopGuard.invalidRetries: Corrective retries must be an integer between 0 and 5
